title: 2023 city budget and tax levy approved
subtitle: Capital forecast, community and economic development grants, library and Centre in the Square funding, debentures, and reserve spending.
overview: Council held a short special meeting to approve the 2023 operating and capital budgets, adopting the Finance and Corporate Services Committee report item by item. The general tax levy was set at $146,507,227, which means an increase of about 4.84% before tax policy changes, with assessment growth of 1.89% included {{vote:m3}}.

Council approved a 2023-2032 capital budget and forecast totalling $1,613,535,000 {{vote:m14}}. It also approved $20,358,000 in capital funded from current revenue for tax-supported operations and $71,721,000 for City enterprises {{vote:m2}}. New debenture financing includes $1,446,000 for City Hall spandrel glass replacement {{vote:m16}} and $2,928,000 for EDIF 2.0 projects {{vote:m17}}.

Residents will see funding continue for the public library, Centre in the Square, Tier 1 community and minor sports grants, and economic development partners. A Councillor declared a conflict on certain community centre and street projects and did not take part in those matters. The meeting adjourned shortly after the by-law was confirmed.

decisions.detail: Council approved a general levy of $146,507,227, about a 4.84% tax increase excluding tax policy changes, including 1.89% assessment growth {{vote:m3}}.
Council approved the 2023-2032 Capital Budget and Forecast with expenditures for all years totalling $1,613,535,000.
Council approved budgets for the building, golf, parking, gas, water, sanitary and storm water enterprises, with combined revenue of $255,415,719.
Council approved $1,625,523 in Tier 1 grants to community groups and minor sports groups.
Council approved economic development grants totalling $1,622,441 to organizations including the Kitchener-Waterloo Art Gallery, THEMUSEUM and the Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony.
Council approved $12,132,850 in operating funding for Kitchener Public Library.
Council approved $2,011,601 in operating funding, with surpluses kept for capital projects and deficits split evenly with the City for this term of Council.
Council approved $1,446,000 in debentures for City Hall spandrel glass replacement, for a term not exceeding 10 years.
